prompt.context_jp: 東京の朝___、いつものように人の流れとともに動き出す。
prompt.prompt_jp: 東京の朝___、いつものように人の流れとともに動き出す。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that frames 'Tokyo mornings' as the topic the narration will describe.

feedback.correct_en: The narration is setting up 'Tokyo mornings' as the broad theme it will comment on — classic topic は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would signal brand-new information being introduced, but here the city morning is the frame, not news. を is a direct-object marker and does not fit.

contrast_examples.en: The Tokyo morning has come. (new event)

prompt.context_jp: 前を歩く年配の女性の背後から、スーツ姿の男___体当たりに近い勢いで肩を当てて追い越した。
prompt.prompt_jp: スーツ姿の男___体当たりに近い勢いで肩を当てて追い越した。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks the suit-clad man as a newly-introduced actor in the scene?

feedback.correct_en: The suit-clad man appears here for the first time as a new figure in the scene — new-information が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would imply the man was already an established topic. に would mark a destination/recipient, not the actor.

contrast_examples.en: That man is an employee. (known topic)

prompt.context_jp: ぶつかっておいて謝りもしない態度に、腹の底で怒り___くすぶりはじめた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 腹の底で怒り___くすぶりはじめた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits for 'anger' emerging as a new sensation?

feedback.correct_en: The anger is arising for the first time — a new state/subject reported with が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would imply anger was already the topic of discussion. で doesn't fit this subject role.

prompt.context_jp: 駅前の広い歩道___、通勤客と観光客とですし詰めになっていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 駅前の広い歩道___、通勤客と観光客とですし詰めになっていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks 'the wide sidewalk' as the topic being described?

feedback.correct_en: The sidewalk is the scene being described — topic は sets it up as the subject of description.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce it as brand-new information, less natural in this descriptive narration. に marks a destination.

prompt.context_jp: 本当に この世を動かしているの___ 実は 影の黒子たちだ
prompt.prompt_jp: 本当に この世を動かしているの___ 実は 影の黒子たちだ
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits the 'it is X (and only X) who really moves the world' identification?

feedback.correct_en: The sentence treats 'the one truly moving the world' as the known topic and identifies it as the shadow figures — は is used in this topic-identification pattern.
feedback.incorrect_en: が here would make the entire nominalized clause a new-info subject, clashing with the 'reveal' structure. を is wrong grammatically.

contrast_examples.en: The one who did it is me. (topic→identify)
I did it. (exhaustive focus on actor)

prompt.context_jp: 光___あれば 闇___ある
prompt.prompt_jp: 光___あれば 闇___ある
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits the existential 'where there is X, there is Y' pattern?

feedback.correct_en: Existence statements with ある typically take が to assert that the item exists. This is the conditional existence pattern.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make them topics, undermining the 'wherever there exists X' logic. に doesn't fit existing items this way.

contrast_examples.en: If there is time, I'll do it.

prompt.context_jp: 先輩の二葉___相変わらず口数少なく、視線ひとつで指示を出す。
prompt.prompt_jp: 先輩の二葉___相変わらず口数少なく、視線ひとつで指示を出す。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks Futaba as the ongoing topic being described?

feedback.correct_en: Futaba is already a known character; は presents her as the topic the narrator is characterizing.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce her as new information, which doesn't fit the ongoing description of a known person.

prompt.context_jp: 重い沈黙のあと、院長の西尾___姿を現した。
prompt.prompt_jp: 重い沈黙のあと、院長の西尾___姿を現した。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks the first appearance of Director Nishio in this scene?

feedback.correct_en: Nishio enters the scene for the first time here — a sudden appearance / new-info が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would imply he was already the topic being discussed. に doesn't mark a subject appearing.

prompt.context_jp: しょうがないのよ ウチ___慶西大医学部 出てないと 立場が弱いから
prompt.prompt_jp: ウチ___慶西大医学部 出てないと 立場が弱いから
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits 'As for our place, if you didn't graduate from Keisei...'?

feedback.correct_en: ウチは sets 'our hospital' as the topic/frame, with the rest commenting on its conditions.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make 'our place' a new-info subject of a single predicate, not a frame-setting topic.

contrast_examples.en: We are the ones at fault. (exhaustive)

prompt.context_jp: ヤツが欲してるの___金じゃない 権力だ
prompt.prompt_jp: ヤツが欲してるの___金じゃない 権力だ
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits 'What he wants is not money—it's power'?

feedback.correct_en: 'The thing he wants' is set up as the topic, then identified — classic nominalized-clause + は pattern.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would turn it into a new-info subject and clash with the 'not X, but Y' identification frame.

contrast_examples.en: Sincerity is what matters. (focus on sincerity)

prompt.context_jp: 診察が急に止まったことへの困惑___、そのため息にもにじんでいる。
prompt.prompt_jp: 診察が急に止まったことへの困惑___、そのため息にもにじんでいる。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks 'confusion' as the newly-described element seeping into the sigh?

feedback.correct_en: The confusion is being pointed out as a perceivable thing in the scene — descriptive が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would elevate 'confusion' to a topic for extended commentary, but this is a one-shot observation.

prompt.context_jp: 人ごみ___は肩がぶつかりがちで、七菜も足を止めながら前へ進んでいく。
prompt.prompt_jp: 人ごみ___は肩がぶつかりがちで、七菜も足を止めながら前へ進んでいく。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks 'the crowd' as the location where bumping tends to happen?

feedback.correct_en: で marks the location where an action/event takes place — here, inside the crowd.
feedback.incorrect_en: に would mark a static existence or destination, not the setting of the action. を marks a direct object.

prompt.context_jp: 院長席の男は、机上のカレンダー___小さく印を書き込んでいた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 机上のカレンダー___小さく印を書き込んでいた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks the calendar as the surface where the mark is written?

feedback.correct_en: 書き込む takes に for the surface the writing is placed onto — a goal/target location.
feedback.incorrect_en: で would mark the general action location, but we need the specific target surface. を marks the object being written, not the surface.

contrast_examples.en: Write using a notebook. (odd — means 'at/with the notebook')

prompt.context_jp: 先ほど あの女性___ わざと ぶつかりましたよね？
prompt.prompt_jp: 先ほど あの女性___ わざと ぶつかりましたよね？
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks 'that woman' as the target of the bumping?

feedback.correct_en: ぶつかる is intransitive and takes に to mark the target you collide with.
feedback.incorrect_en: を would require a transitive verb like ぶつける. で doesn't mark the collision target.

prompt.context_jp: 三好の口___重かったが、湯気とビールに温められて、少しずつ本音がこぼれはじめる。
prompt.prompt_jp: 三好の口___重かったが、湯気とビールに温められて、少しずつ本音がこぼれはじめる。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits 'Miyoshi's mouth was heavy (but)...'?

feedback.correct_en: The contrastive 'but' (が接続) calls for は to mark the topic being contrasted — mouth-heavy initially, then softened.
feedback.incorrect_en: Using subject-が here clashes with the contrastive comment-structure that follows.

contrast_examples.en: He is quiet, but sharp. (contrastive topic)

prompt.context_jp: 七菜は先日助けられた恩を忘れられず、望月千代たちのラーメン屋の話を持ち出したくて___いた。
prompt.prompt_jp: ラーメン屋の話を持ち出したくて___いた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb that captures 'itching / restless with eagerness'.

feedback.correct_en: うずうずする captures the restless itch of wanting to do something immediately — exactly Nana's eagerness here.
feedback.incorrect_en: のろのろ (slow/sluggish) and だらだら (lazy/dragging) describe sluggishness, the opposite of what's needed.

contrast_examples.jp: 話したくてうずうずする。

prompt.context_jp: 「___ほどの者では… ございません」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「___ほどの者では… ございません」
prompt.prompt_en: Fill the set phrase used to politely decline giving one's name.

feedback.correct_en: 名乗るほどの者ではございません is a fixed humble phrase ('I'm not someone worth naming myself').
feedback.incorrect_en: 叫ぶ (shout) and 名づける (name/give a name to) don't form this idiomatic self-effacing phrase.

contrast_examples.jp: 名乗るほどの者ではありません。
子供に名前を名づける。
contrast_examples.en: Give a name to a child.

prompt.context_jp: 「ンン… 先生は___んです」(= was set up / framed)
prompt.prompt_jp: 先生は___んです
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb meaning 'was framed/set up'.

feedback.correct_en: ハメる (to trap/frame) in the passive means 'was set up' — fits the plot where Miyoshi was framed.
feedback.incorrect_en: 褒められた means 'was praised' and 見られた means 'was seen' — neither matches 'framed'.

prompt.context_jp: 「私たちは秘書です 秘密は___まで持っていきます」
prompt.prompt_jp: 秘密は___まで持っていきます
prompt.prompt_en: Complete the set phrase: 'We take secrets to the ___.'

feedback.correct_en: 墓場まで持っていく ('take to the grave') is the fixed expression for absolute secrecy.
feedback.incorrect_en: The idiom specifically uses 墓場; the others don't convey the 'lifelong secret' meaning.

contrast_examples.jp: この秘密は墓場まで持っていく。
contrast_examples.en: I'll take this secret to the grave.

prompt.context_jp: 父親が院長とかやってると ___とか言われてさ
prompt.prompt_jp: 父親が院長とかやってると ___とか言われてさ
prompt.prompt_en: What term accuses a son of riding on his father's prestige?

feedback.correct_en: 親の七光り refers to riding on a parent's reputation — exactly what Naoya resents being called.
feedback.incorrect_en: 下積み means years of hard, unrecognized work. 玉の輿 refers to marrying into wealth (used earlier by another character).

contrast_examples.jp: 親の七光りと言われる。
contrast_examples.en: Called a beneficiary of parental fame.

prompt.context_jp: そんなカス親子がボスなんて ___の労働環境と 言っていいでしょう
prompt.prompt_jp: そんなカス親子がボスなんて ___の労働環境
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word for 'the worst' work environment.

feedback.correct_en: 最悪 ('the worst') matches Saran's scathing judgment of the parent-son duo.
feedback.incorrect_en: 最高 is 'the best', the opposite. 最新 means 'newest', irrelevant.

prompt.context_jp: 「ひ･み･つ･です ___だけに！」
prompt.prompt_jp: ひ･み･つ･です ___だけに！
prompt.prompt_en: Which word creates the pun ('secret' ↔ this profession)?

feedback.correct_en: The joke relies on 秘書 (secretary) sharing the kanji 秘 with 秘密 (secret).
feedback.incorrect_en: Only 秘書 produces the kanji pun with 秘密; 医師 and 看護師 don't share the character.

contrast_examples.jp: 秘書だけに秘密は守ります。
contrast_examples.en: Being a secretary, I keep secrets (pun).

prompt.context_jp: 落ち着き払ったその物腰の裏に、金銭を受け取るような___があるとは、どうしても思えなかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 金銭を受け取るような___があるとは
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the noun meaning 'greed/avarice'.

feedback.correct_en: 欲深さ ('deep greed') fits the accusation of secretly taking money.
feedback.incorrect_en: 優しさ (kindness) and 明るさ (cheerfulness) are positive traits, opposite of the implied flaw.

prompt.context_jp: Saran responds to the director about flowers for the new hospital head.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds most natural as Saran's polite reply to her boss?

choices.text: はい 院長のお名前で お花を お贈りしておきました
うん 院長の名前で 花 送っといたよ
はい 院長の名前を 花に贈りました

feedback.correct_en: (a) uses お-prefix and お〜しておく humble form appropriate for addressing one's boss — the actual line from the story.
feedback.incorrect_en: (b) is casual speech unsuitable for this workplace. (c) is grammatically garbled — you don't 'send the name to the flowers'.

contrast_examples.jp: お贈りしておきました。
contrast_examples.en: I have (humbly) sent it in advance.

prompt.context_jp: Miyoshi declining a gift from a patient.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds most natural for a doctor politely refusing a gift?

choices.text: こういうの ホント 受け取れないんで
こういうの マジむり受け取んないし
このようなものを 受け取る 不可能です

feedback.correct_en: (a) is colloquial-but-professional refusal — softened with ホント and 〜んで, matching the scene.
feedback.incorrect_en: (b) is too slangy/youth-speak for a doctor to a patient. (c) is grammatically unnatural, like a literal translation.

prompt.context_jp: Nana urges Miyoshi not to quit.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing is most natural for 'If you quit, many patients will be in trouble'?

choices.text: 先生が辞めたら 困る患者 たくさんいます
たくさん患者が 困るいます 辞めたら先生
患者たくさんが 先生辞めたら 困ります

feedback.correct_en: (a) follows the natural conditional-then-main-clause order used in the story.
feedback.incorrect_en: (b) and (c) scramble the word order in ways Japanese speakers don't use — the conditional comes first, modifiers precede nouns.

contrast_examples.jp: 辞めたら困る人がいる。
contrast_examples.en: There are people who'd be stuck if you quit.

contrast_examples.jp: 困る人が辞めたらいる。

prompt.context_jp: Saran politely excusing herself to check the hallway.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds most natural as a secretary's polite excuse to her boss?

choices.text: 念のため 調べてきます
一応 ちょっと見てくるわ
念のためだから 調べに行くつもりだよ

feedback.correct_en: (a) is crisp, professional, and matches secretary-to-boss register.
feedback.incorrect_en: (b) is too casual (〜わ ending). (c) is overly explanatory and ends in casual だよ, unfit for her boss.

prompt.context_jp: A secretary declining to reveal her boss's name at a mixer.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds most natural as a polite deflection?

choices.text: それは 守秘義務があるので 言えません
それ 言ったらダメなやつだから 言わない
それは 守秘義務だから 言えるないです

feedback.correct_en: (a) uses the clean professional phrase 守秘義務があるので — natural in a work-adjacent context.
feedback.incorrect_en: (b) is too casual/blunt. (c) contains the ungrammatical 言えるないです (correct form is 言えません).

contrast_examples.jp: 守秘義務がありまして。
contrast_examples.en: I have a duty of confidentiality.
